source: Kaiser, Frigessi, Ramezani-Kebrya, Ricaud (2025) CogniLoad, Appendix A (rho vs d and N)
finding: Gap 2. The paper's own appendix shows by eye that distractor ratio interacts with the other two knobs. Harder puzzles (larger d) deepen the U-shape in distractor ratio. Longer puzzles (larger N) flatten it.
numbers: d=1: shallow dip at rho 25-50%, small recovery by 75%. d=10, mean over rho: GPT-5 0.821, o3 0.804, GPT-5-mini 0.675, o4-mini 0.646, Gemini-2.5-Pro 0.654, DeepSeek-R1-0528 0.475, R1-Distill-Llama-70B 0.361, QwQ-32B 0.300, Qwen3-32B 0.280. N=20: clear U. N=100: strongest models stay between about 0.93 and 0.97 at every rho. N=250: curves flat or rising, at low levels.
quote: increasing d accentuates the classic U-shape
limits: Descriptive reading of mean-accuracy plots only. No interaction term fitted, no test. Output tokens not held equal (32K total context cap, default decoding). 10 puzzles per cell for proprietary models, 100 for open models.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence that the three knobs are not additive: the cost of clutter depends on difficulty and length. A budget built as a plain sum of the three is wrong in the middle of the range.

source: Kaiser et al. (2025) CogniLoad, limitations paragraph
finding: Gaps 1 and 2. The authors state the factorial design supports tests of interactions among d, N and rho, and list that as future work. The paper has only main-effect load-sensitivity regressions.
numbers: Design: 14,000 puzzles per open model (100 per d,N,rho cell); 1,400 per proprietary model (10 per cell). 22 models.
quote: systematically investigate interactions among d, N, rho, which CogniLoad's factorial design supports
limits: No follow-up with interaction terms found in my searches, but the search budget was exhausted, so absence is weak evidence.
agent_relevance: The cleanest open test of our budget question is cheap to run on this public generator: fit accuracy on d, N, rho and pairwise products at a fixed output cap.

source: Modarressi et al. (2025) NoLiMa: long-context evaluation beyond literal matching
finding: Gap 3. On a retrieval-heavy task, more irrelevant text hurts a lot once question and needle share no words. The decline is steady with length, not U-shaped.
numbers: Accuracy 1K to 32K: GPT-4o 98.1, 98.0, 95.7, 89.2, 81.6, 69.7 (base 99.3). Llama 3.3 70B 94.2 to 42.7. Claude 3.5 Sonnet 85.4 to 29.8. Gemini 1.5 Pro 86.4 to 48.2. GPT-4o mini 67.7 to 13.7. 11 of 13 models fall below 50% of their short baseline at 32K.
limits: Varies context length, not the needle-to-hay ratio at fixed length, so it is not a clean test of the U shape. Non-reasoning models in the main table.
agent_relevance: Supports Adapala: on retrieval-style tasks the harm of extra text is graded and monotone, with no recovery. The U-shape may be specific to state-tracking puzzles.

source: Modarressi et al. (2025) NoLiMa-Hard, reasoning models (Table 5)
finding: Gap 3. Reasoning models (o1, o3-mini, R1-distill-70B) on the 10 hardest NoLiMa pairs start near 99% at short length and still fall below 50% at 32K. Reasoning does not remove the length harm on retrieval.
numbers: Short-length scores 98.8-99.9 for the reasoning models; all models below 50% of base at 32K. Llama 3.3 70B without CoT ends at 8.9, with CoT 10.1.
quote: Across all models, performance drops below the 50% mark at 32K context length.
limits: Row labels in the PDF text are scrambled, so I trust only the statement that all models are below 50% at 32K. Subset of 10 needle-question pairs.
agent_relevance: A reasoning-tuned model is not immune to long irrelevant context on retrieval tasks. Keep context lean even for strong models.

source: Hassid, Synnaeve, Adi, Schwartz (2025) Don't Overthink it: preferring shorter thinking chains
finding: Gap 9. In four open reasoning models on four hard benchmarks, within one question the shortest sampled chain is more often right than a random or the longest one. Effortful length is not a sign of correctness.
numbers: Shortest vs random: +2.2 to +15.7 points absolute (math averages). Longest vs random: -5.4 to -18.8 points. Shortest vs longest: up to +34.5 points. Shortest chains 50% and 67% shorter than random and longest. Models LN-Super-49B, R1-32B, QwQ-32B, R1-670B; GPQA-D, AIME24, AIME25, HMMT. 32,768-token cap, temp 0.7. short-1@k uses up to 40% fewer thinking tokens than majority voting.
quote: shorter reasoning chains within individual questions are significantly more likely to yield correct answers
limits: Correlational within question. Unfinished generations excluded (they often loop). Harder questions still need longer chains across questions. Open models only.
agent_relevance: A germane-style reward for long effortful reasoning would be mis-aimed. Length is a weak, often negative, signal of success inside a fixed question.

source: Feng, Kempe, Zhang, Jain, Hartshorn (2025) What characterizes effective reasoning? Length, review, structure of CoT
finding: Gap 9. With question fixed effects, across ten reasoning models on HARP and GPQA-Diamond, longer CoT and more review go with lower accuracy. The share of steps in abandoned branches (Failed-Step Fraction) predicts correctness better, in every model.
numbers: 10 models; 16 CoTs per question for correlation; 64 generations per problem on AIME-25 and GPQA-Diamond for reranking. FSF reranking gives up to 10 points pass@1 gain on AIME; length and review-ratio reranking give less. Claude 3.7 on math is an exception (review ratio helps). Removing failed branches raises accuracy on incorrect traces.
quote: both naive CoT lengthening and increased review are associated with lower accuracy
limits: Graph extraction uses an LLM annotator. Correlations are within question and stronger on harder questions.
agent_relevance: Trace quality (few dead ends) matters, not effort. A cheap dead-end count is a better signal than length.

source: Yoon et al. (2025) Reasoning models better express their confidence
finding: Gap 4. Verbalised confidence from reasoning models is better calibrated than from non-reasoning twins, and sharpens as the CoT unfolds. So a self-rating can predict own errors, but this was not tested with distractor-only changes.
numbers: 6 reasoning models, 6 datasets: strictly better calibration in 33 of 36 settings. GLM-Z1 has 0.07 lower accuracy than GLM-4 on NonambigQA but 0.037 lower ECE and 0.078 higher AUROC. Non-reasoning models get worse Brier score as CoT proceeds.
quote: reasoning models become increasingly better calibrated as their CoT unfolds
limits: Confidence is about answers, not felt difficulty or effort. No manipulation of irrelevant text. Open-weight model pairs.
agent_relevance: A late confidence read after reasoning is more trustworthy than an early one. A gate on a pre-reasoning rating is not supported.

source: Kadavath et al. (2022) Language models (mostly) know what they know
finding: Gap 4. Models can be trained to output P(IK), the chance they know the answer. It rises when relevant source text or a hint is added. That is right for helpful context, but shows the rating moves with context, not only with difficulty.
numbers: 52B model: an obscure question P(IK) 18%; with the relevant Wikipedia article 78% (worked example). On TriviaQA the average gain is larger for shorter articles. P(IK) calibration is weak on new tasks.
limits: 2022 Anthropic models, trained P(IK) head, not a prompted verbal rating. No distractor-only condition.
agent_relevance: A self-difficulty rating is context-sensitive. Validate on distractor-only changes before using it as a gate.

source: He-Yueya, Goodman, Brunskill (2024) Evaluating and optimizing educational content with LLM judgments
finding: Gap 6. GPT-3.5 acting as simulated learners reproduced the expertise reversal effect: worked examples help low-expertise simulated students and make no difference for high-expertise ones. The expertise is a persona, not the model's own strength.
numbers: gpt-3.5-turbo-16k, temperature 0. Expertise reversal and variability effects replicated. Agreement between LM worksheet judgments and human teachers: Pearson r=0.661, p<0.05, n=56 teachers.
quote: both practice and worked-example groups show similar outcomes
limits: The authors admit the model may have seen these findings in training. Not a test of strong versus weak LLMs reading the same extras.
agent_relevance: LLMs can model the effect when told the learner's level; this does not show our agent suffers it. The agent-side question stays open.

source: The few-shot dilemma: over-prompting large language models (2025)
finding: Gap 6. In requirements classification, extra examples help up to about 5-20 shots, then hurt in most models, strong and weak alike. No reversal by strength: the helpful extra turns harmful for GPT-4o too.
numbers: 7 LLMs. GPT-4o, GPT-3.5-turbo, LLaMA-3.1-8B, Gemma-3-4B decline after 5-20 examples; DeepSeek-V3 plateaus; LLaMA-3.2-3B weakens from the start (breaks past 20 examples); Mistral-7B keeps improving with more shots.
limits: One task family (PROMISE requirements). Weighted F1 only. Author names not verified from the text.
agent_relevance: Examples are not free. The turning point depends on the model, so extras need a per-model check, not a rule such as add examples for weak, drop for strong.

source: Mittal (2026) Did you forget what I asked? Prospective memory failures in LLMs, stacking results
finding: Gaps 1 and 8. Task load and number of stacked format constraints compound: more chained problems and more constraints lower compliance together. This is a descriptive sign of non-additivity. The study has no verify state, so gap 8 is not answered.
numbers: o4-mini at N=5 chained GSM8K problems: compliance 55.0% with 0 extra constraints, 32.5% with 3. Chain length alone, o4-mini: 83.6% to 71.1% to 66.7%. DeepSeek falls to 55-65% at N=5; Llama stays 75-95%. Mean output tokens: baseline 538; chained GSM8K-5 about 977-1150.
limits: Greedy decoding, max 2048 tokens. Input and output tokens not equalised between reminder and no-reminder arms. No agent with a verification step was tested.
agent_relevance: Reminders are cheap, but whether they add value once a verify state checks the output is untested. Test at equal tokens.

source: Wang et al. (2026) ToolLoad-Bench: cognitive load framework for tool-use agents
finding: Gap 1. The authors derive that total load is a sum over steps from two assumptions (success falls exponentially with load; steps succeed independently). Additivity is built in, and accuracy is modelled as exp(-(k*Load+b)). Fit is judged only by Hosmer-Lemeshow calibration.
numbers: Hosmer-Lemeshow p-values all above 0.05 (GPT-4o 0.23, Claude 3.7 Sonnet 0.11, Qwen3-8B 0.89); 500 instances. Extraneous load is scored by Gemini-2.5-pro (ambiguity plus distractor tools).
limits: No interaction model compared. A non-significant H-L test cannot show extra terms would not fit better. Extraneous load is LLM-rated.
agent_relevance: Useful form: multiply step success probabilities, i.e. add loads in log-odds. It is additive across steps, not across ICL, ECL and GCL types.

source: Zhang (2025) CLAI and Shang et al. (2026) CoThinker, carried from earlier phases
finding: Gap 5. Not re-opened this session. Earlier pass: CLAI cuts tokens about 36% at equal accuracy on Llama-3-70B; CoThinker gains on LiveBench but loses on instruction-following. Neither was compared with a plain token-budget prompt on tasks the authors did not choose. No newer independent test found.
numbers: CLAI GSM8K 92.3 vs CoT 92.5 at 310 vs 485 tokens. CoThinker: Reasoning vs CoT +5.1 pp (p=.001); near-misses against a stronger baseline p=.63, .16.
limits: Authors picked the tasks. Search coverage after these papers was limited.
agent_relevance: Treat CLT-labelled prompts as one more prompt variant, not as validated.

source: Park (2010) dissertation on additivity of cognitive load factors
finding: Gap 7. Could not open: the repository serves a proof-of-work bot check and returned HTTP 403 to curl. No numbers retrieved. No later replication found.
limits: Source blocked; do not cite figures from Park.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 stays open. Do not use Park for any threshold.

source: Search record: LLM expertise reversal by model strength
finding: Gap 6 marker. A web search plus reading d09 and d10 found no paper that varies model strength and tests whether helpful extras hurt strong and help weak models.
numbers: Zero direct tests found; two adjacent ones (simulated learners; over-prompting).
limits: Absence from a short search; search budget exhausted.
agent_relevance: Open; cheap to test in our own harness.

source: Search record: self-rating of difficulty versus distractors
finding: Gap 4 marker. No paper found that asks for a difficulty or effort rating and changes only distractors to check for leak. Calibration work (d07, d08) covers answer confidence, not felt effort.
agent_relevance: Do not use a self-rated effort gate until checked in our harness.
